title: Esther 9
paragraphs: ¹ On the thirteenth day of the twelfth month — the month of Adar — when the king's command and decree were about to be carried out, the very day on which the enemies of the Jews had hoped to overpower them, everything turned around: the Jews overpowered those who hated them. ² Throughout every province of King Ahasuerus, the Jews gathered in their cities to attack whoever sought to harm them. No one could stand against them, because all the peoples were afraid of them. ³ All the provincial officials, the satraps, the governors, and the king's administrators helped the Jews, because fear of Mordecai had fallen on them. ⁴ Mordecai had become powerful in the king's palace, and his fame was spreading throughout all the provinces — for he was becoming greater and greater. ⁵ The Jews struck down all their enemies with swords, killing and destroying them, doing as they wished to those who hated them.

⁶ In Shushan the palace, the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men. ⁷ They also killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, and Aspatha, ⁸ Poratha, Adalia, and Aridatha, ⁹ Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vajezatha — ¹⁰ the ten sons of Haman son of Hammedatha, the enemy of the Jews. But they did not lay their hands on the plunder.

¹¹ That same day the number of those killed in Shushan the palace was reported to the king. ¹² The king said to Queen Esther, "The Jews have killed and destroyed five hundred men in Shushan the palace, including Haman's ten sons. What must they have done in the rest of my provinces! Now what is your further petition? It will be granted. What more do you request? It shall be done." ¹³ Esther answered, "If it pleases the king, give the Jews in Shushan permission to do tomorrow what they did today, and let Haman's ten sons be hanged on the gallows." ¹⁴ The king commanded this to be done, and the decree was issued in Shushan. Haman's ten sons were hanged. ¹⁵ The Jews in Shushan gathered again on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar and killed three hundred more men in Shushan, but again they did not lay their hands on the plunder.

¹⁶ Meanwhile, the rest of the Jews throughout the king's provinces had gathered to defend themselves. They gained relief from their enemies and killed seventy-five thousand of those who hated them, though they did not touch the plunder. ¹⁷ This was on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar. On the fourteenth day they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness. ¹⁸ The Jews in Shushan, however, had assembled on both the thirteenth and fourteenth days, and they rested on the fifteenth day and made that a day of feasting and gladness. ¹⁹ That is why the rural Jews — those living in villages and unwalled towns — celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month of Adar, making it a day of gladness and feasting, a holiday for giving gifts of food to one another. ²⁰ Mordecai recorded all these events and sent letters to all the Jews throughout the near and far provinces of King Ahasuerus,

²¹ calling on them to observe every year both the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month of Adar ²² as the days when the Jews got relief from their enemies, and as the month when their sorrow was turned into joy and their mourning into celebration. He told them to observe these days with feasting and gladness, giving gifts of food to one another and presenting gifts to the poor. ²³ So the Jews committed themselves to continuing what they had started, as Mordecai had written to them. ²⁴ For Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them and had cast the Pur — that is, the lot — to crush and destroy them. ²⁵ But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by written decree that the evil scheme Haman had devised against the Jews should come back on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.

²⁶ These days were called Purim, from the word Pur. Therefore, because of everything written in this letter — and because of what they themselves had witnessed and what had happened to them — ²⁷ the Jews established and committed themselves and their descendants and all who joined them to observe these two days every year without fail, in the way prescribed and at the time appointed. ²⁸ These days were to be remembered and observed in every generation, by every family, in every province, and in every city. The days of Purim would never cease to be observed among the Jews, and the memory of these events would never die out among their descendants. ²⁹ Then Queen Esther daughter of Abihail, along with Mordecai the Jew, wrote with full authority to confirm this second letter concerning Purim. ³⁰ Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews in the hundred and twenty-seven provinces of Ahasuerus' kingdom — letters of peace and assurance —

³¹ to confirm the observance of these days of Purim at their designated times, as Mordecai the Jew and Queen Esther had decreed, and as they had established for themselves and their descendants — including the obligations of fasting and mourning. ³² Esther's decree confirmed these regulations about Purim, and it was recorded in a book.
